data.narrative:
Fire Point, a Defense & Security company at Series A stage, is evaluated against a comparable universe of four same-sector, same-stage private companies alongside two public defense technology firms (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). The private peer set spans a wide valuation range from Stark Defence at $4.0B to NODA AI at $125M, with additional context from companies including Anduril Industries and Castelion.

A peer-median approach anchored to the four directly comparable Series A defense companies yields a valuation of $700M. This method reflects the midpoint of a $125M to $4.0B range, with the median pair (Castelion at $1.0B and Singularity at $400M) providing central tendency. The substantial spread between floor and ceiling valuations—a 32x range—reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity, customer traction, and go-to-market positioning typical of early-stage defense investing. Only one triangulation method is applicable given available data constraints, limiting cross-validation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $595M to $805M, centered on $700M. Key uncertainties include Fire Point's specific revenue traction with the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense (anchor investor), product differentiation relative to the broad peer set, and defensibility in an increasingly crowded defense tech landscape. The wide peer valuation dispersion suggests stage-comparable companies command highly heterogeneous valuations; placement within the $595M–$805M band depends materially on Fire Point's customer concentration, retention metrics, and near-term scaling trajectory.
